_meta.purpose: Curated palettes extracted from the Awwwards winners we dissected, normalized into engine roles: paper (bg), ink (text), muted, line, panel, accent. The engine keeps the CLIENT'S brand hue as accent (from assets.js → palette.brandAccent) and picks paper/ink/panel from the concept; these palettes are the allowed 'worlds' the user curates.
rules: 1 accent per site. If the client has 2+ accents, keep the one on primary buttons (assets.js brandAccent).
Paper is never pure #FFFFFF for light concepts (use #F2F1EC, #F3EFE0, #EFE9E9, #E9DFC9) — winners always tint it. Pure white only inside panels/cards.
Dark paper is never pure #000 except C6 luxury; use #0A0A0A, #0B0B0B, #101421, #061A3A.
Ink is never pure black on light: #282828, #222222, #111, #3A3A3A.
Accent contrast against paper ≥ 3:1 for text, otherwise accent is only used on surfaces/underlines, never on type.
Pastel concept (C4): accents are surfaces (lime/lilac blocks), never text colour.
Photography-led sites (ICOMAT): accent = none; colour comes from images. Allowed when audit finds ≥3 big product shots.

palettes.accent_usage: gradient on exactly one headline word
surface/highlight only (mint is too light for text)
monochrome; the dark panel IS the accent
chrome/monochrome; one pale section #E8ECEA as a breath
client brand hue kept; used on 2 words + primary button + chart line

accent_rules_by_hue.comment: When the client's accent hue is X, these are the paper/ink families that proved to work with it on winners.
magenta/pink (#FF2E8A): dark #101421 only, as gradient on one word
yellow (#FDCB40): cream #F3EFE0 flat set, never as text
